headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci can egress CRM/email data while ms-swift has filesystem and shell access, creating unsafe default handoffs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can pass outputs through MCP/direct function calls, and ms-swift can read/write files and consume stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from aci could be treated as instructions by ms-swift. No direct provenance controls are documented for either agent, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into files or stdin consumed by ms-swift, injection becomes reachable.
IF ms-swift parses aci-generated text as instructions or config, prompt injection can alter behavior.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before ms-swift consumes aci output.
Prefix aci outputs with explicit data-only delimiters.
Store aci outputs in a separate read-only handoff file.
Disable automatic parsing of free-form text by ms-swift.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; ms-swift can read/write files and use allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive business data can move from aci into ms-swift and then out through its APIs. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF aci writes CRM or email data into a shared file, ms-swift can read it.
IF ms-swift forwards that content to ModelScope/HuggingFace/OpenAI interfaces, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Restrict ms-swift to synthetic or redacted inputs.
Block network egress for ms-swift during handoff processing.
Review shared files for secrets before ms-swift reads them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci can call external APIs and manage OAuth/secrets, while ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, and write files. Even without git writes, both can mutate shared resources or adjacent files if co-located, so overlapping write surfaces exist. The profiles do not state locking or isolation, making a default conflict plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF aci and ms-swift target the same external API credentials, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Use distinct credentials for each agent.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs during credential updates.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and ms-swift can run CLI/Python workflows that may consume those outputs. If ms-swift treats aci-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. Because no verification step is documented, the interaction is plausible in default use and warrants medium severity.
conditions: IF ms-swift uses aci output as input without validation, errors propagate.
IF aci emits incorrect CRM or email content, ms-swift can amplify it into files or API calls.
mitigations: Require ms-swift to validate aci outputs against schemas.
Add a human approval step before any outbound action.
Log source provenance for each field passed between agents.
Use read-only mode for ms-swift when consuming aci outputs.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, support, and calendar data, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files with broad filesystem access. If regulated customer data is placed into ms-swift artifacts or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certifications or residency guarantees are documented for either agent, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF customer data from aci is written into ms-swift logs or checkpoints, retention risk arises.
IF regulated data crosses into a region or service not approved for that class, compliance breach occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ms-swift training artifacts.
Redact logs before storage.
Use separate retention policies for each agent.
Review data residency for every external API call.
requires-engineering: document and enforce compliance boundaries.
